subject: geography
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which is a likely environmental impact of large-scale deforestation?
options: More carbon dioxide released and increased soil erosion
questions.explain: Cutting and burning trees releases stored carbon dioxide and exposes soil to erosion, while reducing biodiversity.

questions.q: In a food chain, the arrows point in the direction of:
options: The movement of predators towards prey
The flow of energy from one organism to the next
questions.explain: Arrows in a food chain show the direction in which energy is transferred, from the organism being eaten to the one eating it.

questions.q: Which of these is an opportunity provided by a hot desert environment?
questions.explain: The intense, reliable sunshine of hot deserts makes them ideal for generating solar power.

questions.q: Which is a challenge of developing a cold environment such as Alaska?
options: Excessive rainfall causes flooding all year
questions.explain: Permafrost, extreme cold and remoteness make construction, transport and working conditions very difficult in cold environments.

questions.q: Many rainforest leaves have drip tips. What is their main purpose?
options: To allow heavy rain to run off quickly
To store water for the dry season
questions.explain: Drip tips channel the frequent heavy rainfall off the leaf, preventing rot and the growth of fungi and algae.

questions.q: Which of these is a sustainable way to manage a tropical rainforest?
options: Banning all local people from the forest
questions.explain: Selective logging removes only some mature trees and allows the forest to recover, making it more sustainable than clear-felling.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the climate of a tropical rainforest?
options: Hot and dry all year round
Hot and wet all year round
Cold and dry all year round
Hot in summer and cold in winter
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests near the Equator are hot and wet throughout the year, with no distinct dry season.

questions.q: Hot deserts are best described as having:
options: Low rainfall and large daily temperature ranges
Constant cloud cover and high humidity
questions.explain: Hot deserts receive very little rain (under 250mm a year) and have hot days but cold nights, giving a large daily temperature range.

questions.q: Which of the following is a leading cause of deforestation in the Amazon rainforest?
questions.explain: Cattle ranching, along with logging, mining and farming, is a major direct cause of Amazon deforestation.

questions.q: Why do many tall rainforest trees have buttress roots?
options: To support their height in thin, shallow soils
To reach sunlight at the forest floor
questions.explain: Buttress roots are large above-ground roots that give tall trees extra stability in the rainforest's thin, nutrient-poor soils.

questions.q: How is a camel adapted to survive in a hot desert?
options: It has thick blubber to keep cool
It stores fat in its hump and can go long periods without water
It has webbed feet for swimming
It hibernates through the hottest months
questions.explain: A camel stores fat (not water) in its hump and can tolerate large water losses, helping it survive desert conditions.

questions.q: Which biome is typically found in a broad band around the Equator?
questions.explain: Tropical rainforests are located close to the Equator, where high temperatures and heavy rainfall occur all year.

questions.q: Which adaptation helps a cactus survive in a hot desert?
options: A thick, waxy stem to store water
Broad, flat leaves to catch rain
questions.explain: A cactus stores water in its thick, waxy stem and has spines instead of leaves to reduce water loss.

questions.q: What is the difference between a food chain and a food web?
options: A food chain shows decomposers but a food web does not
A food web shows many interconnected food chains in an ecosystem
A food web only shows plants
A food chain is larger than a food web
questions.explain: A food web links together many food chains, showing the complex feeding relationships within an ecosystem.

questions.q: What does the term 'biodiversity' mean?
options: The variety of living organisms in an area
The average temperature of a biome
The total amount of rainfall in an area
The number of rivers in a region
questions.explain: Biodiversity is the variety of plant and animal species found in a particular ecosystem or on Earth as a whole.

questions.q: Which human activity is a major threat to global biodiversity?
questions.explain: Destroying habitats removes the homes of plants and animals, reducing the variety of life (biodiversity).

questions.q: What is the role of producers in a food chain?
options: They recycle nutrients into the soil
They convert sunlight into energy by photosynthesis
questions.explain: Producers such as green plants make their own food from sunlight through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain.

questions.q: An animal that eats only plants is best described as a:
questions.explain: A herbivore is a primary consumer that feeds only on plants (producers).

questions.q: In a tropical rainforest, the dense, continuous layer of treetops that blocks most light from reaching the ground is called the:
questions.explain: The canopy is a thick layer of treetops about 30–45m up that absorbs most of the sunlight and rainfall.

questions.q: A large ecosystem covering a wide area, such as tropical rainforest or tundra, is called a:
questions.explain: A biome is a very large-scale ecosystem, such as desert or rainforest, defined mainly by its climate and vegetation.

questions.q: Why is the soil in a tropical rainforest often surprisingly infertile?
options: Heavy rain leaches nutrients and most nutrients are stored in the vegetation
It is too cold for plants to grow
questions.explain: Most nutrients are held in the biomass; heavy rainfall quickly leaches the thin soil, so it is rapidly exhausted once trees are cleared.

questions.q: How are plants such as lianas and epiphytes adapted to life in the rainforest?
options: They climb or grow on other trees to reach sunlight
They lose their leaves in winter
They have thick fur to keep warm
They store fat to survive droughts
questions.explain: Lianas climb up tree trunks and epiphytes grow on branches, both reaching the light without making their own tall trunks.
